findings.summary: Pub/sub row is inconsistent: Kafka consumer groups are placed as pub/sub examples although the page defines queue as one consumer per message, which blurs the model.
findings.evidence: Examples | SQS, RabbitMQ queue | SNS, Redis pub/sub, Kafka groups (full copy each)
findings.fix: Move Kafka to a separate note: 'Kafka: queue within a group, pub/sub across groups'.

findings.summary: The claim that min.insync.replicas=2 means losing one broker loses no data leaves out the replication factor it depends on.
findings.evidence: With min.insync.replicas=2, losing one broker loses no data
findings.fix: State the assumption: with replication.factor=3, acks=all and min.insync.replicas=2, a write is acknowledged only after at least 2 replicas have it. Losing one broker then loses no acknowledged data, and the partition stays writable. With RF=2, losing one broker makes writes fail.

findings.summary: The replication claim leaves out the replication factor, so the durability setup looks complete when it is not.
findings.evidence: "With min.insync.replicas=2, losing one broker loses no data" and the config block with only acks=all and min.insync.replicas=2
findings.fix: State that the topic needs replication.factor=3. With a factor of 2 and min.insync.replicas=2, losing one broker blocks writes instead of surviving. Add replication.factor=3 to the properties block.
